title: Unbiased Canary Deployments & Metric Evaluation
prompt: An e-commerce checkout service deploys a 5% canary (v2.8) behind an AWS ALB configured with target-group sticky sessions (`stickiness.enabled=true`, 24-hour cookie `AWSALB`). Automated canary analysis (Kayenta/Argo Rollouts) passes v2.8 after 30 minutes because error rate is 0.01% and p99 is 42 ms. Upon promoting v2.8 to 100%, authenticated checkout fails at 14% with a `NullPointerException` on saved payment tokens. Investigation reveals v2.8 only received 0.4% of traffic—exclusively new anonymous visitors—while 99.6% of returning authenticated users were pinned to Baseline by the 24-hour sticky cookie. Design a bias-free canary routing and statistical evaluation pipeline.

spark.summary: A 5% canary deployment received 0.4% of actual requests—all new/anonymous users—because ALB sticky sessions pinned 95% of returning authenticated users to Baseline.
spark.keyTakeaway: Eliminate session-affinity skew by using stateless services with JWT/Redis sessions, request-level weighted routing, and stratified canary evaluation.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A checkout service (`4,000 RPS`, `85%` returning authenticated users, `15%` new visitors) deploys a `5%` canary (`v2.8`) behind an AWS ALB with `stickiness.enabled=true` (`24h` `AWSALB` cookie).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts 24h AWSALB Cookie Starves Canary of Returning Authenticated Users (85% Returning Auth -> ALB (Sticky=ON) -> Baseline (v2.7) -> Canary (v2.8, 5%)); Stateless L7 95/5 Split + Shared Redis + Stratified Gate (4,000 RPS (85% Auth / 15% Anon) -> L7 Weighted / User-ID Hash -> Shared Redis / JWT Session -> Kayenta / Argo Stratified Gate).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Shortening `AWSALB` cookie TTL from `24 h` to `1 h` still starves a `30-minute` canary window. Eliminate selection bias with zero user logouts: **Externalize Session State**: Store sessions in Redis/ElastiCache or stateless JWTs so any request can route between Baseline and Canary seamlessly.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Cohort-stratified progressive delivery is standard in high-volume SaaS and e-commerce: **Argo Rollouts & Flagger**: Uses Envoy/Istio weighted routing paired with Prometheus cohort queries.

learningJourney.title: Selection bias, underpowered metrics, and post-promotion outages
learningJourney.explanation:
Session-affinity skew ruins automated canary analysis in two ways:

1. **Cohort Selection Bias**: Authenticated code paths (`auth_state=authenticated`, 85% of revenue) are effectively untested during the 30-minute canary window.
2. **False Statistical Confidence**: Global `0.01%` error rate looks green while authenticated errors are masked by sample-size starvation.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Stateless Redis/JWT Sessions + Stratified L7 Canary
learningJourney.explanation:
Eliminate selection bias with zero user logouts:

- **Externalize Session State**: Store sessions in Redis/ElastiCache or stateless JWTs so any request can route between Baseline and Canary seamlessly.
- **Per-Request L7 Weighted Splitting (or `hash(user_id)`)**: Disable `stickiness.enabled` and use Envoy/Gateway `95/5` weighted clusters (or deterministic `hash(x-user-id) % 100 < 5` if multi-step UI affinity is needed).
- **Cohort-Stratified Kayenta / Argo Gates**: Require minimum sample size (`N >= 10,000` requests per cohort) and evaluate `error_rate` and `p99` separately for `auth_state=authenticated` and `auth_state=anonymous`.

            terminal: true

learningJourney.title: Where unbiased canary evaluation protects progressive delivery
learningJourney.explanation:
Cohort-stratified progressive delivery is standard in high-volume SaaS and e-commerce:

- **Argo Rollouts & Flagger**: Uses Envoy/Istio weighted routing paired with Prometheus cohort queries.
- **Feature Flag & A/B Experimentation**: Uses deterministic `hash(user_id)` bucketing to prevent sticky-cookie skew.
- **Zero-Downtime Checkout Releases**: Validates authenticated payment paths at 1–5% before full rollout.
